references.text: The description of how the menorah (lampstand) was to be made from pure gold, which is the background for it being called 'the pure lampstand' in Leviticus 24:4.
The command that Aaron and his sons shall keep the lamps burning before the Lord's presence from evening until morning, which expands on the requirement to tend the lamps 'continually' (tamid).
Aaron is to tend the lamps every morning and evening, which elaborates on the daily service of the lampstand before the Lord.
Mentions 'the pure lampstand' (hamenorah hatehorah) using the same terminology as in Leviticus 24:4.
Refers to 'the pure lampstand' and its lamps, which were made according to the Lord's command.
Instructions for Aaron to set up the seven lamps so that they shine toward the front of the lampstand.
The Levites keep the lamp lit every evening on the golden lampstand, showing the continued practice of tending the lamps before the Lord.
Mentions the lampstand in the holy place of the tabernacle as part of the description of the earthly sanctuary and its service.
John sees seven golden lampstands, drawing symbolism from the golden menorah in the tabernacle.
The seven burning flames before the throne symbolize God's Spirit and connect to the lamps that were to burn continually before the Lord's presence.
